summary: Set structure now follows the company's Payslip components: monthly CTC plus per-employee overrides of those components (the fixed Basic/HRA/LTA/PF template is gone in v2). Monthly CTC is pre-filled from the annual CTC on the employee record. CTC must be 1–1,00,00,000; overrides cannot be negative and percentages cannot exceed 100; a set whose earnings exceed CTC or whose deductions exceed gross is refused. Only active employees (not candidates) can get a structure, and the run sheet lists only employees.
testSteps: 1. Log in as HR. 2. Payroll > pick an employee > Set structure. Expected: Monthly CTC pre-filled (annual CTC ÷ 12), a table of the company's components with "inherit" boxes, grade shown read-only from the designation, live breakup on the right. 3. Enter CTC 50,000 > Save. Expected: saved, row shows ₹50,000.00.
negativeTests: 1. CTC -1000 > Save. Expected: "Monthly CTC cannot be less than 1". 2. Basic override 150. Expected: "Basic Salary cannot be more than 100". 3. PF override -5. Expected: "Provident Fund cannot be less than 0". 4. A candidate (Offer sent) is not in the list; via API: 409 "A salary structure can only be set for an active employee…".
automated: scripts/v2/test-payroll.js — section "Salary structure follows payslip components"
v1Impact: v1 PUT/GET /api/admin/salary-structure unchanged (asserted); new behaviour is on the v2 route only.

summary: Generate draft now validates every input: days paid 0–days in the month, arrears/bonus/TDS non-negative and at most ₹1 crore, and a draft whose net pay would be negative is refused. Publish, Publish all, Delete and Regenerate ask for confirmation. Published payslips are locked: "Unpublish" is replaced by "Revert to draft", which requires a reason and records who/when/why (payslips.revert_reason). The Year list is dynamic (two years back to next year).
testSteps: 1. HR > Payroll > a closed month > employee > Generate, leave fields blank > Generate draft. Expected: draft created. 2. Publish > confirm dialog > Publish. Expected: status Published, row shows "Revert to draft" (no Unpublish). 3. Revert to draft > reason "Wrong arrears" > confirm. Expected: back to Draft. 4. Delete a draft > confirm dialog appears first.
negativeTests: 1. Days paid 45 (30-day month). Expected: "Days paid cannot be more than 30". 2. Arrears -1000. Expected: "Arrears cannot be less than 0". 3. TDS 99999999. Expected: "TDS cannot be more than 1,00,00,000". 4. TDS 90,00,000 on ₹50,000 CTC. Expected: "Net pay would be ₹-… — deductions are more than the earnings…". 5. Revert to draft with an empty reason. Expected: "Give a reason…".
automated: scripts/v2/test-payroll.js — "Generate validation, publish lock and month-end"
v1Impact: v1 generate/unpublish unchanged (asserted: 45 days accepted, unpublish without reason works).

summary: Increments now have maker-checker: whoever recorded a revision cannot approve it ("You recorded this revision, so someone else must approve it."). A revision can only be applied on or after its effective date, so a December revision no longer changes November payroll. Errors show inside the New revision form next to the field and the form stays open with the input kept. Apply/Cancel are dialogs (and row-level errors show under the row).
testSteps: 1. Log in as Company Super Admin > Increments > New revision > TH5001, Effective 01-12-2026, New annual CTC 3,60,000 > Record. 2. Approve (same user). Expected: error under the row "You recorded this revision, so someone else must approve it." 3. Log in as HR > Approve > confirm. Expected: Approved. 4. Apply. Expected: "This revision takes effect on 01-12-2026. Apply it on or after that date…"; payroll CTC unchanged.
negativeTests: 1. Same-user approve → 403 message above. 2. Apply before effective date → 409 message above. 3. Invalid input keeps the form open with field errors.
automated: scripts/v2/test-payroll.js — "Increments: validation, maker-checker, effective date"
v1Impact: v1 approve/apply unchanged (asserted: recorder can approve, future revision applies on v1).

summary: F&F can only be created for an employee with an approved resignation or termination (others get "A Full & Final settlement can only be made for an employee whose resignation or termination has been approved."). LWD must be ≥ joining date; all amounts/days must be ≥ 0. Drafts can be edited and deleted (with confirmation). The engine no longer pays a day when LWD is before DOJ, and the leave encashment bug (SUM of a non-existent balance column → always 0) is fixed.

summary: Letters have rules per type: Relieving/Experience only after an approved exit (LWD taken from that record and locked), Promotion/Increment only off an applied revision (pre-filled from it — the employee record is changed through Increments, not by a letter), Confirmation and others only for active employees. Every field is typed (date pickers, CTC number, designation from the master, choices) and validated server-side; any missing field, including the signatory, stops the issue with field errors. Issued letters can be revoked with a reason (PDF stamped REVOKED). Reference numbers are sequential per organisation per year (e.g. TH/LTR/2026/0007).
testSteps: 1. HR > Letters > Issue a letter > Relieving Letter. Expected: only employees with an approved exit listed; LWD pre-filled and greyed. 2. Fill signatory > Generate > confirm. Expected: issued with a sequential reference. 3. Revoke > reason > Revoke. Expected: status Revoked.
